lines: It flexed where it should and held where it had to. Good work saves skin.
The scuffs show where you took the hardest hits.
That left strap stretched, but it never tore.
Mud under the buckle means this was used far from a clean road.
The stitching held through more strain than I would ask of it twice.
One edge is worn smooth from drawing the same tool again and again.
I can replace the cracked section without rebuilding the whole piece.
Whatever struck here nearly cut through both layers.
The fit has changed since you first wore it.
Bring this back after I oil it and reset the fastenings.
The sweat marks tell me it stayed on through a long fight.
Someone patched this in a hurry, and the patch somehow held.
That buckle saved the rest when the leather started to pull.
The gear did its job. Now it needs a day on my bench.
I would not trust the frayed thread through another battle.
These scratches are shallow, but this split near the edge is not.
You kept it clean enough that I can see the real damage.
The right side took most of the wear. Does that match the fight?
I can mend the torn lining before it rubs you raw.
This came home used, not ruined. That is a good report.
No scuffs yet. I appreciate gear that does not rush to prove itself.
The surface is clean enough that I can still see my finishing marks.
Nothing here says it has met a real fight.
Try every buckle before you need to fasten it in a hurry.
The leather is still stiff from sitting unused.
Walk in it for a while before trusting the fit.
A clean edge tells me nothing about how it handles a hard pull.
The straps have not stretched to your shape yet.
I would rather adjust this now than during an emergency.
Storage kept it dry, but one fold has begun to set.
The stitching looks sound. Use will give the honest answer.
Make sure you can reach every fastening with cold hands.
There is dust under the collar and no dirt on the outside.
Oil it before the first long trip, not after.
A shelf cannot tell us where this will rub.
The lining is untouched, so wear it around the village first.
Nothing has failed because nothing has tested it.
The fit matters more than how new it looks.
Keep it ready, but do not call it proven yet.
Bring it back after its first outing and I will check what changed.
